submitter: bugs_open/440 lane, round 1 — phase 1a of RFC_062 (the spec.reason routing/annotation split). 440 was spun out of bugs_closed/410's candidate 1 by owner decision 2026-09-02; it continues the deferral bugs_open/404's own livespec header states ('splitting annotation from routing key is the real repair and is RFC-scope'). This submission is the INERT foundation only: one new livespec module plus tests, zero callers, zero behaviour change. The phase-3 guarantee change (the gate refusing a present-but-unknown routing key) is NOT in this submission — it goes through RFC_062 and its own round.
rationale: The estate cannot refuse an unknown re-render reason today because spec.reason is two fields wearing one name: the gate's routing key AND a free-prose annotation. [MEASURED 2026-09-02] 11 distinct values on live page_rerender items, including free prose minted THE SAME DAY by migrations 696/693 (which bypass the Go creator entirely, so 404's loud-warning guard — probe-verified in today's binary — has fired ZERO times in production; the first count said 2 and both rows were council payloads quoting the string, WRONG_CALLS 2026-09-02), a deliberate assemble-only key (verbatim_adoption_deploy), and routing-SHAPED unknowns (tool_retirement x16, light_palette_chrome_replaced x13) that silently assembled. Migration 696 proves intent is unrecoverable from the data: it updated content_data AND rendered_html together so its assembles are CORRECT, while an author who edited only content_data would mint identical rows whose assemble re-ships the stale artefact. The split gives intent a place to live: spec.routing_reason carries only vocabulary values, spec.reason stays free forever, and present-but-unknown becomes a mistake BY CONSTRUCTION — refusable with no legitimate counter-example. THIS submission ships only the foundation: the spec-key constant, a closed three-state resolver (absent->assemble, known->sections, unknown->refuse — the enum shape makes 'unknown but proceed' unrepresentable at the type level), and the two clause renderers later migrations will paste (established CheckRerenderModeConditionClause idiom). Opt-in, unsafe default OFF (owner 2026-08-02 section 2); zero live consumers, enumerated not asserted (grep -rn RoutingReasonSpecKey returns the definition and tests only) — NOT architecture-scope per RFC_022's three-condition test, while the phase-3 flip IS and is documented as such in RFC_062.

plan.summary: One new file in platform/livespec (the routing-key constant, the three-state resolver, two paste-target clause renderers, a header pinning the opt-in/RFC status and the missing-key-vs-empty evaluator caveat) plus its test file (refusal proven with REAL observed unknowns from the census; the annotation-only boundary pinned; clauses derived from the vocabulary by loop so they cannot drift; both mutations named and killed). A REB-008 register entry ships in the same commit (ordering-exemption condition 2), stating BUILT-AND-INERT explicitly so the register cannot overstate it.

Header states: inert, zero callers, default OFF, RFC_062 owns the flip, and the missing-vs-empty evaluator caveat that must be confirmed before any paste.

Discharges 410's inherited verification trap: the refusal is proven with REAL observed unknowns (tool_retirement, light_palette_chrome_replaced — the census's own silently-assembled keys), not a synthetic value alone; the absent->assemble boundary is pinned so a future over-strict edit fails against the migration-696 population; clause tests iterate the vocabulary so a sixth value cannot silently be missing; the known-clause is asserted to NEVER test the annotation field.

The seam registered in the same commit that ships it (ordering-exemption condition 2). Status says BUILT AND INERT BY DESIGN with the do-not-overread warning, because a register status that outlives its truth is a documented landmine.

plan.risks: (1) A mechanism with zero callers can rot unexercised — the estate's own objection. Mitigated by design: it is the stated phase-1a of an owned, planned RFC with the consumer list and phases written (RFC_062, lane PLAN), not a speculative helper; the register entry says INERT explicitly so nothing overstates it. (2) The clause renderers could be pasted before the evaluator's missing-key behaviour is confirmed — stated as a blocking caveat in the file header, the RFC's open list, AND this risks block; phase 3 cannot pass its own round without discharging it. (3) platform/livespec currently carries a pre-existing RED (TestNoNewMigrationFileReadersOutsideTheAllowList, the 405 lane's committed breakage, unchanged 7 days, documented in 404's NOTES) — this submission's four tests pass and the failure reproduces identically WITHOUT these files; stated so the package-level FAIL is not read as this change's. (4) Cross-lane surface: the module extends the 404 lane's vocabulary file's PACKAGE but touches none of their files; CONTRIB posted in their NOTES (commit 5b5c669dd) before this submission, and phase 1b (their creator file) is explicitly gated on their lane reading its r4 verdict.
